title: barbarahelena/metagenomicspipeline pipeline parameters
description: shotgun metagenomics pipeline to obtain relative abundances and pathway abundances

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: A comma-separated file with a header row and the columns `sample`, `fastq_1`, `fastq_2` (empty for single-end reads) and optionally `run_accession`. A sample sequenced in several runs gets one row per run, with the same `sample` and a different `run_accession`; use `--perform_runmerging` to merge them. Relative paths are read relative to the launch directory, or else relative to the samplesheet's folder.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome for removing host reads: give --fasta, --bowtie2_index or --genome.

genome.errorMessage: The genome name must not contain spaces and must be a valid identifier.
genome.help_text: If using a reference genome configured with iGenomes (not recommended), provide the ID for the reference (e.g., `--genome GRCh38`). This builds paths for all required reference files. See the [nf-core documentation](https://nf-co.re/usage/reference_genomes) for details.

fasta.description: Path to the host reference genome FASTA, used to build a Bowtie2 index for removing host reads.

bowtie2_index.description: Path to a directory with a prebuilt Bowtie2 index (*.bt2) of the host genome. Takes precedence over --fasta.

igenomes_base.description: The base path to the igenomes reference files

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`.

skip_preprocessing.description: Skip all preprocessing (quality filtering, host read removal, run merging, subsampling); FastQC still runs.

skip_qualityfilter.description: Skip quality filtering and adapter trimming with fastp.

skip_hostfilter.description: Skip host read removal with Bowtie2.

skip_subsampling.description: Skip subsampling of the reads to --subsamplelevel.

skip_kraken.description: Skip taxonomic classification with Kraken2 and Bracken (skipped by default; use --skip_kraken false to run it).

skip_shortbred.description: Skip ShortBRED quantification of antibiotic resistance genes (CARD markers; skipped by default).

adapterlist.description: FASTA file with adapter sequences for fastp. Without it, fastp detects adapters itself.

save_trimmed_fail.description: Keep the reads that fail fastp filtering (in the fastp task folder).

fastp_cutright.description: Trim reads from the 3' end with a sliding window (fastp --cut_right).

fastp_meanquality.description: Mean quality the sliding window must reach (fastp --cut_mean_quality).

fastp_length.description: Minimum read length after trimming; shorter reads are discarded (fastp --length_required).

perform_runmerging.description: Merge the runs of a sample (samplesheet rows with the same sample name) after host read removal.

subsamplelevel.description: Number of reads (pairs) to subsample each sample to. Samples with fewer reads are kept as they are.

publish_mergedreads.description: How host-filtered and merged reads are saved to the output directory. They are large, so they are symlinked to the work directory by default.

humann_db.description: UniRef protein database for HUMAnN: uniref90_ec_filtered_diamond, uniref90_diamond, uniref50_diamond or uniref50_ec_filtered_diamond.
humann_db.help_text: You can choose one of the following: uniref90_ec_filtered_diamond (default), uniref90_diamond, uniref50_diamond, uniref50_ec_filtered_diamond

kraken2_db.description: Path to a Kraken2 database folder. When not given, the prebuilt database --kraken2_dbname is downloaded.

kraken2_dbname.description: Prebuilt Kraken2 database to download when --kraken2_db is not given.

kraken2_save_reads.description: Save the classified and unclassified reads from Kraken2.

kraken2_save_readclassifications.description: Save the Kraken2 classification of every read.

bracken_build.description: Build the Bracken files for --bracken_readlength (bracken-build), e.g. for a custom Kraken2 database. The prebuilt databases include them for common read lengths.

bracken_readlength.description: Read length for Bracken; the database needs a matching database<length>mers.kmer_distrib file.

bracken_threshold.description: Minimum number of reads a taxon needs before Bracken re-estimates its abundance.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
Options that change how the pipeline runs, rather than what it computes.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.
